notes: The part type arduino-nano-33-ble-sense is the catalogue match given for the Nano 33 IoT. Its port names are assumed to follow the Nano convention (A4, A5, 3.3V, GND.1). The diagram's '3V' label is mapped to 3.3V.

The circuit image shows the boards, resistors and wires with no breadboard drawn. The parts list includes mini breadboards, so one breadboard (bb1) is used to join the shared SCL and SDA lines and the two 4.7k pull-up resistors. Only one is used, although the list names two.

Image wiring: GND to GND, A5 to A5 (teal, SCL), A4 to A4 (yellow, SDA). Each of the A4 and A5 lines has a 4.7k pull-up to the 3V line from the reader's 3V pin. The teal and yellow lines cross without connecting. The manual says SDA is A4 and SCL is A5.
Both boards are powered and programmed over USB from the computer. USB cable ports are unspecified, so those edges have no ports and are joined only.
The manual lists 10 jumper wires, but the circuit needs only 6. The extra wires are unused.
Rail holes tp.1, tp.10 and tp.14 are chosen arbitrarily. All top-positive rail holes are one strip, so the pull-ups share the 3V rail.
